dedupe_keys.name: cadence 125 million call disconnection events from consumer android devices march to june 2024

description: CaDENCE, published by researchers of the Universidade Federal do Amazonas in Brazil, is an event-level dataset of 125,532,358 call disconnection records collected by device software on consumer Android smartphones over 98 days, from 9 March to 14 June 2024. Each record is one call termination with its time, pseudonymous device and software identifiers, mobile network codes, radio access technology, band and channel, signal quality (RSRP and RSRQ), service-state flags and a label telling dropped calls from normal terminations. The release used a daily capped export that favoured dropped calls, so the label mix is not the true drop rate; aggregate counts of the source warehouse are given to document this. Coverage: the devices' networks (mobile network codes identify operators; the countries were not read); 2024. Format and access: one ZIP of about 0.5 GB on Zenodo, free of charge for non-commercial use under CC BY-NC 4.0. Caveats: sampling favours drops; devices are app users, not a random sample; no locations. Simulation uses: rates and radio conditions of dropped calls for service reliability and degradation models of mobile networks, and training of failure predictors. Related records: the Slovak RAN performance counters give the network side; CRAWDAD holds older device traces.
